newsitem.title: UK: Sedgwick pofits up, says confident of 1997.
newsitem.headline: Sedgwick pofits up, says confident of 1997.

text.p: British based insurance broker Sedwick Group on Wednesday reported a five percent increase in full-year profits and said it was looking forward to 1997 with confidence.
Pre-tax profits for the twelve months to December 1996 rose to 95.5 million pounds on brokerage and fees up four percent at 914.9 million pounds.
Sedgwick chief executive Sax Riley said that excess capacity in the industry had now become the norm and that the group had further developed its strategy of diversifying into fee-based opeartions.

"Our strategy is not based on false hopes for an improvement in the rating environment, but on developing and changing our business to, and profit from, prevailing and future market conditions," said Riley.
Earnings per share fell to 11.6 pence per share from 12.6 pence the previous year reflecting the low tax rate in 1995.
The underlying dividend was held steady at 6.5 pence per share for the year and including a foreign income dividend enhancement was 7.25 pence per share.
